statement: For a rooted tree with offspring a_i in {1,2}, bond p>0, m_i=p^i product_(j<i)a_j, terminal survival q_n=1 and S_n=sum_(i<n:a_i=2)1/m_i, one has 1/m_n+S_n/4 <=1/q_0<=1/m_n+S_n/[4(1-p/2)].
assumptions: independent bond variables on disjoint descendant subtrees
proof: Direct subtraction 1/[2pq(1-pq/2)]-1/(2pq)=1/[4(1-pq/2)] and telescoping with weights 1/m_i; full reproduction in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: No gap in this tree lemma. No graph-with-loops extension follows.

statement: The explicit bounded-degree trees T_beta of w438 have p_c=1/sqrt(2) and critical root survival iff beta>1; T_0 and T_2 are quasi-isometric with equal p_c but opposite critical behavior, and finite-prefix periodic-tail approximants can die at criticality while converging locally to T_2.
proof: Floor derivative and bounded-gap estimates, reciprocal identity, suffix criterion, and corridor contraction reproduced in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: Does not establish or refute P0043 because all example trees fail quasi-transitivity. C05 had no second peer audit in this packet.

statement: For uniform L-subdivision T_L of the 3-regular tree, p_c=2^(-1/L), sup_L P_pc(o reaches fixed radius n)=1, and at fixed L the critical one-arm probability q(kL) satisfies (kL)q(kL)->6L while critical susceptibility is infinite.
proof: Independent coarse-edge reduction, forward recursion u_(k+1)=u_k-u_k^2/4, reciprocal increment limit 1/4, root three-arm formula, and shell expectation 3/2; full reproduction in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: No uniform graph-independent decay follows; fixed-graph extinction is already known in this exponential-growth family. Parent conjecture remains unproved here.

statement: For m>=2, let D_m be the graph obtained by replacing each edge of the infinite 3-regular tree by m internally disjoint paths of length two. Under iid Bernoulli bond percolation, p_c(D_m)=sqrt(1-2^(-1/m))<1, critical percolation has no infinite cluster almost surely, and for an original vertex o, lim_(k->infinity)(2k)P_pc(o connects to graph distance 2k)=12.
assumptions: each edge block has fresh internal vertices
proof: Each finite diamond block is usable with independent probability r_m(p)=1-(1-p^2)^m. Infinite clusters correspond exactly to those of the 3-regular skeleton. The skeleton threshold is r=1/2, yielding p_c. At r=1/2 forward survival u_(k+1)=u_k-u_k^2/4; reciprocal increments tend to 1/4, so k u_k->4. Root three-arm probability q_(2k)=1-(1-u_(k-1)/2)^3 gives k q_(2k)->6 and (2k)q_(2k)->12. Inserted vertices occur at odd distance only.
remaining_gap: Independent review of block equivalence, exact radius parity and constant. This exponential-growth special case does not address the subexponential parent gap.
